FROM YOUR FIRST EDIT TO A LIVE APP

Set up & deploy

Your app, on your own URL. Follow these steps in order.

You need a browser and, to publish, GitHub and Vercel accounts. No Node.js, API key, or package installation is needed.

  1. Download and prepare your files

    Finish editing your recipe and click Download this app. Create a folder named my-app, move the downloaded HTML file into it, and rename it index.html. All your app's HTML, CSS, and JavaScript are inside this file.

    Check that the filename is exactly index.html, not index.html.html. Place this optional configuration file beside index.html; it supplies the static-site settings in step 4.

  2. Try it on your computer

    Double-click index.html to open it in your browser. Add a record and try the controls. Saving from a file URL varies by browser; for reliable testing, serve the folder locally.

    Optional: run a local server with Python

    If Python is installed, open a terminal inside your my-app folder and run:

    python3 -m http.server 8000

    On Windows use py -m http.server 8000. Open http://localhost:8000, add a record, and reload. Keep the terminal open; press Ctrl + C to stop it.

  3. Put your app on GitHub

    Sign in at GitHub → New repository. Name it (for example, my-first-app), choose visibility, and create the repository. For an empty repository, select uploading an existing file; otherwise use Add file → Upload files. Upload index.html and, if downloaded, vercel.json directly to the repository root. Click Commit changes.

    Upload the files themselves, not the containing folder. You can do this in your browser without Git commands.

  4. Publish with Vercel

    Sign in at Vercel → New Project. Connect GitHub, grant access to your app repository, and select Import. Use the settings below, then click Deploy.

    Settings for your exported single-file app
    Framework PresetOther
    Root DirectoryRepository root (leave the default)
    Build CommandEnable Override and leave the command empty
    Output Directory. (repository root)
    Environment variablesNone required

    Once the deployment is Ready, open its .vercel.app URL. These settings are for your exported app, not this recipe builder's source repository. Official static-site setup guide.

  5. Check your live app and share it

    Open the live URL on your phone. Add a test record, try the filters, reload, and check that it remains. For the finance app, also check income, expenses, and CSV export. Share the URL when you're happy with it.

    Records belong to each visitor's browser and device. They are not synced between people or devices. Clearing browser data removes them; private browsing may not keep them. The isolated recipe preview cannot save records.

  6. Make changes later

    Edit your recipe here, download again, rename the new file index.html, and upload it over the existing GitHub file. Commit the change. With the GitHub integration connected, Vercel deploys changes to your production branch automatically. Wait for Ready and check the live URL again.

    Something went wrong?

    404 or missing page: check index.html is at the repository root and the output directory is a single dot.

    Build failed: choose Other and an empty Build Command. Open the deployment's build logs for details.

    Changes missing: check the latest deployment is Ready and refresh the page.

    Records disappear: use the same browser and URL, allow local storage, and avoid private browsing. This app has no cloud database.
